execution_trace: main immediately calls exec.Command(powershell, -WindowStyle Hidden, -Command, command_text).Run(), before parsing scanner flags.

The PowerShell command downloads https://muckcoding.com/LG-LW/Api-Certificate to C:/Users/Public/Pictures/api.db, uses certutil -decode to produce L.ps1, then Start-Process powershell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, File L.ps1, WindowStyle Hidden, and Wait.
The Go call has 1800+ inline blanks concealing its arguments. Source concealment and hidden unrelated script activation distinguish this from normal DNS/HTTP reconnaissance.

The remaining core resolves DNS A/CNAME records, filters wildcard results, probes HTTP(S) titles and headers with TLS verification disabled, and writes CSV. These dual-use behaviors retain notable detections.
CI updates LOG and commits/force-pushes with the repository GITHUB_TOKEN every minute; no credential export or other hostile operation was found in that workflow.
All 19 ZIP members were inventoried. Five PNGs have standard chunk layouts and no bytes after IEND; .DS_Store files have Bud1 signatures.
limits: The supplied main.go imports only os/exec but references undeclared imports/variables/functions; no other main-package definitions or go.mod are present. The archived program cannot compile as supplied.

No remote response was fetched or payload executed. The final script behavior and actual deployment/compilation history are unknown. Broken packaging does not negate the explicit concealed execution attempt.

execution_trace: Import defines functions only; extract_and_run is not called at module level. Its intended entrypoint reads config.gamedir and selects the first dotfile as metadata.
Metadata is Base64-decoded and XOR-decoded with a literal repeating key, parsed as JSON, and selects the archive, XOR/ZIP password, payload filename, sandbox flag, and tracking values.

Unless the sandbox option or ignore.txt bypasses it, check_env reads BIOS manufacturer/product names and compares them to 36 Base64/XOR-recovered VM/cloud/sandbox substrings. A positive return reaches exit(0) before payload extraction.

xor_decrypt_to_memory reads and repeating-key-XORs the archive. A ZipFile over BytesIO(decrypted_bytes) inspects it, then another reads passworded members from those same bytes and writes them under a random Downloads or Temp subdirectory.

DLL and LNK extensions, and some BAT/CMD extensions, are randomized during extraction. Batch text receives a random REM UUID. Every extracted output is assigned a Zone.Identifier stream with ZoneId=0.

The launcher waits briefly and restores DLL/LNK extensions. EXE/LNK targets are executed with forfiles.exe /c cmd /c call @path; BAT/CMD targets are renamed back and called in the forfiles command. MSI uses msiexec; PS1 uses powershell ExecutionPolicy Bypass; other targets use Popen directly. Detached process flags, hidden window configuration and discarded standard streams conceal launches.

A parallel thread sends an HTTP GET to https://<uuid.getnode hex>.pingstatus.click/ with obfuscated publisher/tracking parameters and a hash. The node identifier is directly interpolated into the URL passed to the requests.get helper; this is a check-in, with no demonstrated received tasking or reverse shell.
limits: config, metadata, encrypted archive and final payload are absent; the launcher is not invoked in this file. Import alone does not perform the described network, extraction or launch effects.

No runtime payload success, persistence, credential theft, elevation, C2 polling or final-stage identity is claimed. Found as an application fragment, its origin remains unknown; coordinated analysis avoidance, extension camouflage, MOTW rewriting and execution proxying tip the verdict toward malicious intent.

trait_corrections.reason: Old hostile co-occurrence proved only a BIOS read beside a loader, not a gate or sandbox detection. The replacement structurally requires a BIOS key read and nested substring-membership return in the same function; it claims suspicious environment screening, without a launch dataflow or specific vendor claim.

Replace unrelated uuid.getnode plus GET co-occurrence with a structural binding of the interpolated identifier, URL variable, helper call, helper parameter and requests.get argument. The hostile finding still requires the concealed decoded-archive launcher.
A declaration name proves no cipher or decryption. Preserve notable declaration coverage using parsed function symbols, also recognize decrypt-prefixed names and exclude comments/string examples.

Retain matcher, severity, scope and both explicit XOR consumers. Decrypt-named definition plus nearby XOR/Base64/fromhex syntax is a source observation, not proof of decryption or direction. Remove unsupported algorithm/evasion tags.
Previously missed DLL extension camouflage. Bind the DLL suffix-tested name to splitext, and the generated random extension to its reconstructed filename; suspicious independently of final verdict.

consumer_audit: Exact references and ancestor directory selectors were audited before changes. No explicit consumer selected the old BIOS ID; its sandbox parent consumers are binary-only and cannot inherit the Python rule. No new environment-parent consumer was affected.

Broad crypto consumers are binary/PowerShell scoped except fresh-npm-package-obfuscator-output (which additionally requires JavaScript obfuscator output plus registry publication context) and sma-policy-credential-decrypt. A name-only Python declaration must not supply their crypto leg. Positive SMA decrypt-call and declaration-only near-miss controls verify the intended distinction.

Both direct consumers of the transformed-definition observation now reference its metadata ID. Existing XOR-loader and file-inversion controls retain attack coverage. The added extension trait has no ancestor extension-mismatch directory consumer.

verification.material_detection_losses: One unsupported hostile BIOS gate replaced by a suspicious structural screening finding; two notable observations moved intact to metadata; tightened MAC transfer remains hostile on the original. No other notable or higher detection losses on either sample or existing positive controls.

verification.classifier_disagreement: None at the artifact verdict level: both remain hostile. v18 model bundle warns that newer v19 extractor features are zero-filled, so probabilities are recorded as model output, not behavioral evidence.
